title: An E^r first-intersection block for r>=2 produces a two-sided envelope that is not trailing-evens / the expanding-prefix test / the archived OE corridor
statement: After odd-run interiors push to the peak and even-run interiors push to the next valley, classifying the first intersection by the length r of the common E^r suffix produces an O E^r O envelope, or an emptiness for r>=2, that is not cycle_trailing_evens_lt / odd_preimage_unique / power_bound_word plus even_run_scale_barrier / corridor_bounds / ee_entry_count n(n^2+n+1), and that type empties or tightens a bound for a reason that is not an archived cell.
counterexamples: r=1 outer cell is n^4 <= u^3 < (n+1)^4, the archived OE corridor
first-run O^{a0} E^r is CycleMin-possible iff 2^{a0+r} <= 3^{a0} (power_bound_word plus even_run_scale_barrier); (2,2) and (3,2) fail, (4,2) and (6,3) hold
25 --OOOEE--> 15 realizes r=2 after a short climb by dropping below n
last-run r>=2 is occupied: n(n^2+n+1) EE chains and a trailing-EEE witness; 115 with a0=5, r=2, valley 8165 is CycleMin-shaped
notes: Phase 0 only. Not a reopen of the eight-case intersection table, the OE corridor, or the cyclic seam. The envelopes are REPARAMETERIZATIONs of trailing-evens and the expanding-prefix test. No finance, no K=11, no L=55293, no floor raise. No Paper A edit, no ledger row, no new Lean. Not a halt theorem.
tested_range: n=10^6+1 envelopes and last-run occupancy; a0<=8, r<=6 prefix table; realized OO-launches on odds in [13,2001); witnesses 25 and 115
